article.title: The Sixteenth Floor Dream Journal
article.description: Pavan (29, Infosys) & Shruti Kulal's (28) first-home search on outer Sarjapur Road and Hosa Road — stretching from ₹1 Cr to ₹1.44 Cr, surviving a RERA stall, a ₹50K exit, and the country's most anxious spreadsheet, eight months before their first child arrives.

tabs.description: Getting to know Pavan (29, senior engineer at Infosys) & Shruti Kulal (28, QA lead) — first-generation city-property buyers from Udupi and Davangere, deploying ₹22L savings into a primary 2BHK, with a baby arriving as their real possession deadline.

buyers.name: Pavan Kulal
buyers.description: First-generation buyer carrying a ₹70L home loan decision the way his father carried co-operative bank ledgers. Every stalled-project story lands in his chest; every Sunday site visit ends at a darshini.

buyers.name: Shruti Kulal

roadmapNodes.title: L1: The Fridge That Started It
roadmapNodes.desc: The landlord's 10% hike letter and the pregnancy test share a fridge magnet; 'GHAR — FINAL' v1 is born in the kitchen.

roadmapNodes.title: L2: The TRUTH Column
roadmapNodes.desc: The asterisk education: base → all-in ≈ +16–18%. The TRUTH column instituted beside the brochure prices.

roadmapNodes.title: L3 DETOUR: The Neopolis Ad
roadmapNodes.desc: Sobha Neopolis full-page — the Greek dream with its bougainvillea showflat. ₹2.3–2.72 Cr reality; one fight, one dosa, a 'DREAMS — PARKED' sheet invented.

roadmapNodes.title: L4 REGRESSION: The Chandapura Grief
roadmapNodes.desc: The widening to Attibele-Chandapura; Shruti's one-line veto on a sticky note: 'a home, not a point proven to two fathers.'

roadmapNodes.title: L5 DETOUR: The Value Mirage
roadmapNodes.desc: Godrej Splendour 2BHK from ₹85L all-in — dies on an 8:15 am drive test: 1h50m to Electronic City.

roadmapNodes.title: L6: The Booking Summit
roadmapNodes.desc: Hosa Rd under-construction 2BHK booked at ₹1.22 Cr, CLP, 10% paid — the happiest evening of the entire search.

roadmapNodes.title: L7 BOUNCE: The RERA Flatline
roadmapNodes.desc: RERA quarterly progress flat-lines; 2 am buyers'-group archive session; exit fought, refund minus ₹50K 'administrative charges.'

roadmapNodes.title: L8: Chirping Woods Close
roadmapNodes.desc: Ready-with-OC pivot (GST math seals it): Shriram Chirping Woods 2BHK, ₹1.44 Cr all-in; CIBIL-ghost wobble; registration at week 32 on the eight-months bump.

quotes.text: Everyone says buy. Nobody says how to stop being scared.
quotes.author: — Pavan

quotes.text: The ad was built by professionals to find exactly you — eight weeks pregnant, tired, deserving one beautiful thing. It worked because you're human, not because you're foolish.
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: A home, not a point proven to two fathers.
quotes.author: — Shruti

chatMessages.text: Riya, don't laugh. The showflat had bougainvillea, marre. Actual bougainvillea. I was standing in that Santorini balcony thinking this is it.
I'm not laughing. That ad found exactly you — tired, deserving one beautiful thing. We don't delete the dream — we park it. Dreams with numbers stop whispering.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “They are the cohort the market has been cruellest to — the ₹95L 2BHK they saved toward in 2024 simply no longer exists. And yet every Sunday, one project, one spreadsheet, one argument, one dosa. The Excel version number kept climbing and the fear never left, but neither did they. When the RERA stall hit, they didn't freeze — they exited with ₹50K worse and refocused on ready-with-OC math. That pivot, made eight months pregnant, is the steel this journal is built on.”

chatMessages.text: We booked one flat, lost ₹50K to a RERA stall, and somehow ended up in a ready-with-OC community. Is that the most expensive lesson or the cheapest?
The cheapest. ₹50K for a lesson that will protect every property decision you make for thirty years. And the GST math on ready-with-OC paid for it twice.

tabs.description: Key takeaways for first-generation buyers navigating the first-EMI fear, RERA vigilance, and the baby-as-deadline clock.

lessons.title: The RERA portal is genuinely readable.
lessons.description: Registration number, possession date, complaint history, quarterly updates — twenty minutes per project replaced hours of WhatsApp-forward anxiety with actual facts.

lessons.title: Construction-linked payment plans are the first-timer's friend.
lessons.description: 10% at booking, the rest following slabs, means savings deplete with the building's actual progress, not before it — until the progress stops.

beforeItems.text: Brochure possession date is as good as a guarantee
The per-sqft price is the real price of the flat
A bigger flat is always better for a growing family

differentlyCards.title: Check RERA updates monthly from booking
differentlyCards.description: Setting a calendar reminder for the first of every month would have caught the flat-line sooner and possibly saved the ₹50K.

differentlyCards.title: Compute all-in cost from visit one
differentlyCards.description: Opening the TRUTH column before the first site visit would have eliminated price-sheet hope-and-crush cycles.

differentlyCards.title: Model the worst-month buffer earlier
differentlyCards.description: Writing the layoff+EMI+infant survival number before booking would have shaped the 2BHK vs 2.5BHK decision with data, not dread.

differentlyCards.title: Pivot to ready stock sooner
differentlyCards.description: The GST math and possession-certainty case for ready-with-OC was hiding in plain sight — they wish it had been month 3's discovery, not month 6's rescue.

chatMessages.text: We started at ₹1 Cr and ended at ₹1.44 Cr. We booked one flat. We exited one flat. We survived a flat-line and a ₹50K toll. Is that winning?

Your father built his Udupi house room by room over nine years, loan-free. You built a home in eight months, through a stall, at 32 weeks pregnant — with the spreadsheet versioned seven times and the emergency fund still intact. That's not winning; that's a generation's leap completed.

tabs.adviceStoryboardImagePrompt: A vector storyboard showing Pavan and Shruti opening the RERA portal, parking the Neopolis dream, receiving the flat-lined progress chart, and registering Chirping Woods at week 32, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with a Warm Coral #FF8A65 focal accent, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background.
tabs.adviceDescription: For first-generation buyers deploying combined adult savings into a primary home, the edge is not in finding the cheapest per-sqft — it's in reading the RERA portal monthly, computing the all-in cost honestly, and pricing the worst-month survival buffer before the offer. Pavan and Shruti proved that a ₹50K exit is cheaper than a stalled possession, and that ready-with-OC plus nil GST math is the first-timer's insurance policy.

monthlyLearnings.headline: The RERA portal is genuinely readable — 20 minutes per project
monthlyLearnings.body: Registration number, possession date, complaint history, quarterly updates — twenty minutes per project replaced hours of WhatsApp-forward anxiety with actual, checkable facts.

monthlyLearnings.headline: Construction-linked payment plans are the first-timer's best friend
monthlyLearnings.body: 10% at booking, the rest following construction slabs, means savings deplete with the building's actual progress — not in a lump sum before a single brick is laid.

monthlyLearnings.headline: The anxious middle tier of builders sorts itself by delivery history
monthlyLearnings.body: They learned to filter less by brochure quality and more by a single question: has this builder delivered two projects on time? Two delivered projects on time beats one celebrity architect, every time.

monthlyLearnings.headline: The 2.5 BHK costs the emergency fund — the convertible study won
monthlyLearnings.body: Priced the bigger flat honestly for the first time: it empties the savings. The 2 BHK with a convertible study preserves the six-month airbag, and the baby's room still exists — Shruti's choice, with the spreadsheet closed.

monthlyLearnings.headline: GST on under-construction vs ready-with-OC changed the entire comparison
monthlyLearnings.body: 5% GST on UC versus nil on ready-with-OC altered the all-in math more than any developer discount. They now compute all-in cost per project, not per-sqft price — a rule they'll carry into every future purchase.
